stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «Separate channels mean an attacker who steals the password still lacks the second factor, preserving independence.» Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: El indicio de este ítem es «Explain why 2FA should use separate channels / Ask what independence requires. / Two-factor authentication and the second factor». ¿qué opción lo cumple?

answer.exemplar: Separate channels mean an attacker who steals the password still lacks the second factor, preserving independence.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: channel separation preserves factor independence. On that basis "Separate channels mean an attacker who steals the password still lacks the second factor,…" is the supported choice.
questions.hint: Ask what independence requires.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: A phishing message and the signals in it
questions.learningObjective: Recognise a phishing signal in offers

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: «An unsolicited prize demanding financial details.» « You have won a £500 voucher. Claim now by entering your bank details » La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: Aplicando «Recognise a phishing signal in offers / Ask what the email demands and whether it was solicited. / A phishing message and the…» al texto, ¿cuál de las opciones se sostiene?

options.misconception: mistakes a surface feature of "Vouchers are always scams" for the governing rule

options.text: An unsolicited prize demanding financial details

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: an unsolicited prize demanding bank details is a phishing signal. On that basis "An unsolicited prize demanding financial details" is the supported choice. Option A ("The amount is too small") fails because it judges the prize size; Option C ("Vouchers are always scams") fails because it mistakes a surface feature of "Vouchers are always scams" for the governing rule; Option B ("Emails are never legitimate") fails because it dismisses all email.
questions.hint: Ask what the email demands and whether it was solicited.

questions.topic: Public wireless and its specific risk
questions.learningObjective: Identify a safe alternative to public Wi-Fi

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «Use a personal hotspot or VPN.» Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: Con la pista «Identify a safe alternative to public Wi-Fi / Ask how to avoid the open network. / Public wireless and its specific risk», ¿qué opción se ajusta realmente al fragmento?

options.text: Use a personal hotspot or VPN
Post them on a shared drive publicly

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: a personal hotspot or VPN protects the files. On that basis "Use a personal hotspot or VPN" is the supported choice. Option C ("Email them unencrypted") fails because it creates a new exposure; Option B ("Use the airport's open Wi-Fi") fails because it exposes the files; Option D ("Post them on a shared drive publicly") fails because it destroys confidentiality.
questions.hint: Ask how to avoid the open network.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: A strong password and why length beats complexity

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: «Use long, unique passphrases stored in a manager.» La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: Con «Summarise password best practice / Combine length, uniqueness and safe storage. / A strong password and why length beats…» presente, ¿qué respuesta se desprende de la nota?

options.text: Write passwords on paper for safety
options.misconception: reverses the direction of the reasoning the passage sets out

options.text: Use short complex passwords reused across sites
Use long, unique passphrases stored in a manager

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: long, unique passphrases in a manager is best practice. On that basis "Use long, unique passphrases stored in a manager" is the supported choice. Option A ("Write passwords on paper for safety") fails because it reverses the direction of the reasoning that settles a strong password and why length beats complexity; Option B ("Use short complex passwords reused across sites") fails because it reverses best practice; Option C ("Use personal details for memorability") fails because it uses guessable information.
questions.hint: Combine length, uniqueness and safe storage.
